title: af/doctor@3
description: `af doctor --json` (ADR-0210): one token-free health check of this machine and, when it runs in a git repository, that repository. Each check is `ok`, `warn` or `fail`. A check that is not `ok` carries its `fix`, the one command a shell runs as given (several joined by `&&`), never prose, and a `hint` with what the command cannot say: a placeholder's choices (`SHELL`, `DIR`), a step to take first, what the command does. A problem no single command fixes, or one whose command a file that does not load would stop, has a null `fix`, and its `hint` says what to do. Version 1, whose `fix` mixed commands and prose and which had no `hint`, is neither printed nor read. Checks appear in this order, `project` only inside a repository: `harness`, `sandbox`, `network` (diagnostic environment markers only), `binary` (the running af, its install receipt and how it was verified, the default link), `path` (the default link's directory on PATH, and whether `af` on PATH is that link), `shell` (completions and man pages for $SHELL), `update` (the cached release check, a newer release, the policy, the release source's anonymous reachability), `tools` (git >= 2.30, curl, minisign, gh when curl is missing, and what the repository's Gate runs), `providers` (the registry, each registered Provider's login from the token-free status probe, logins found but not registered), `storage` (what af keeps against `[storage] max_bytes`, free disk against `min_free_bytes`, abandoned install stagings), `project` (`.af/` validating, the lock's af pin, each Gate command, a Provider for every model Worker kind). `exit_code` is 1 when any check failed and 0 otherwise, the command's own exit code. The command never calls a model, logs in, installs or writes a file. Version 3 adds harness, sandbox, and network diagnostic checks before binary (ADR-0249); versions 1 and 2 are neither printed nor read.

fix.description: The one command that fixes what the check found, exactly as a shell runs it: an `af` command, an install command or the PATH line for the shell `$SHELL` names (`export PATH='DIR':"$PATH"` for bash, zsh and sh, `fish_add_path 'DIR'`, `set paths = ['DIR' $@paths]` for elvish, `$env:PATH = 'DIR' + [IO.Path]::PathSeparator + $env:PATH` for pwsh, the directory quoted as a literal), several joined by `&&`, an upper-case placeholder (`SHELL`, `DIR`) named in `hint`. It is offered only when running it can clear the check: null when the check is `ok`, on a problem no single command fixes, and when a file the command reads does not load (the error the check reported would stop it); `hint` then says what to do, naming the file and the parse error's line.

hint.description: What the fix cannot say: a placeholder's choices, a step to take first, what the command does, or, without a fix, what to do; null when the check is `ok`.
